commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Brazil IEEPA exception was gated on `not entry_is_line_b`, a positional flag for the witness's single aluminum exemplar line with no basis in the cited heading, instead of the §232 aluminum membership the source carve-out names.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 48 (diff read individually; identical hunks). Only differences are the chapter-prefixed steel parameter name and cosmetic serialization (`effective_from:` ordering vs `from:`, redundant paren count).
triage.verifier_justification: The refutation attempt fails on the source text: HTS chapter 99 U.S. note (x)(vii) states "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02", and 9903.85.02 in the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap) reads "products of aluminum provided for in the tariff headings or subheadings enumerated in subdivision (g) of note 19" — i.e. a §232 aluminum membership, not a line position. Pre-fix, both IEEPA component formulas gated that carve-out on `not entry_is_line_b`, the hand-built witness's exemplar-line flag (its only other use in the module is as the body of `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded`, sourced to a different heading, 9903.01.33), so in a schedule-wide generated chapter module the condition had no source grounding and the fix re-grounds it on `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` — the untraceable_branch pattern ("re-grounds it"), not an added clause or a rename. The module's own unchanged summary already asserted that "section-232 aluminum/steel ... identifiers are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation", so the pre state contradicted its own declared input surface, and the commit's report confirms the intent: "Direct component-formula exemplar references are gone except the intentionally retained beer/section-338 `entry_is_line_d` slots." The other half of the diff (9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02) is provenance only and does not carry the verdict.

triage.verifier_notes: Four things a reviewer should weigh. (1) Split diff: the steel half is mechanical — `ch50_s232_steel_heading_rate` keeps `formula: '0.50'` and `section_232_steel_component_rate` keeps its formula byte-for-byte; only the proof-atom `corpus_citation_path`/`source` strings move from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02. I checked the pinned corpus: 9903.81.87 and 9903.81.88 have no rate rows in 2026-08-03-rulespec-hts-current-with-legacy-aluminum.jsonl while 9903.82.02 does, carrying exactly "Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 50%", so the report's "the task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage" holds and this is provenance, not fidelity. (2) Strongest argument against confirming: in chapter 50 (silk) both predicates are extensionally empty — no silk line is the witness's line b (7601.10.30.00, ch76) and none is §232 aluminum — so no ch50 output value changes; the correction is textual/structural here and materially behavioral only in metals chapters. I still confirm because the rubric keys on encoded meaning (formula and input surface both changed), and the pre-fix module demanded an input with no source semantics whose false default applies the Brazil surcharge to aluminum articles the note exempts. (3) Alternate kind: wrong_entity_or_scope is arguable (the carve-out covered the wrong population), but untraceable_branch is tighter — the predicate itself was a witness artifact re-grounded on the heading the source names. (4) Provenance of the defect: the pre state is the immediately prior commit in the same stack (a9562cfd4 "b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces", PR #1300), so this is an intra-PR self-correction that never reached main; if the corpus is meant to hold shipped defects, prune on that ground rather than on the substance. Note also that `entry_is_line_b` survives post-fix as the body of `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` (line 1925), so the exemplar-flag problem is only partly swept — a related, still-open issue, not part of this diff.
